test_title: PYST 16: SSC GD - GA & GK (Held on: 24th November 2021 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following statements about Emperor Ashoka is FALSE?

options.text: Ashoka was opposed by a wise man named Chanakya (also known as Kautilya).
Ashoka belonged to the Mauryan dynasty.
The empire that Ashoka ruled was founded by his grandfather.
Ashoka is the only king in the history of the world who gave up conquest after winning a war.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka was opposed by a wise man named Chanakya (also known as Kautilya). **__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka was not opposed by a wise man named Chanakya (also known as Kautilya). **
 
• Ashoka belonged to the Mauryan dynasty.
 
• The empire that Ashoka ruled was founded by his grandfather.
 
• Ashoka is the only king in the history of the world who gave up conquest after winning a war.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __**Facts about Ashoka**__

 
• **In 304 BCE**,** Bindusara and Maharani Dharma** or Shubhadrangi gave birth to **Ashoka in Patliputra.**
 
• He was known as **Samraat Chakravartin, Devanampriya, and Priyadarsin.**
 
• From the Hindu Kush Mountains in Afghanistan to Bangladesh, and from Assam in the east to Kerala and Andhra Pradesh in the south, he was in charge of a vast landmass. He died in 232 BCE. King Ashoka had an important role in Indian history and culture. 
 
• In Sanskrit, the word** "Ashoka" means "without sorrow." **The grandfather of Ashoka was the founder of the Maurya Dynasty.
 
• According to the Tibetan writer Taranatha, Ashoka murdered his six brothers to seize the throne of Magadha.
 
• Ashoka was also known a**s "Chandaashoka". **
 
• Ashoka became a follower o**f Buddha after the war of Kalinga in BC 261.**
 
• He made Buddhism his state religion.
 
• He was appointed as the** "Dharma Mahapatro’** to spread Buddhism all over Asia.
 
• He sent his daughter Sanghamitra and son Mahinda to Ceylon to propagate Buddhism.
 
• He built the **lion stambh's-Ashok Stambh to spread Buddhism. **
 
• The Ashok Stambh of Sarnath was accepted as the** national emblem of India.**
 
• Apart from Ashoka Stambh, Ashoka had built many pillars, rock edicts like Bharhut stupa, Dhamek Stupa, and Mahabodhi Temple.
